message.content:
**Order result:** Filled — bought 5 shares of COST at $892.00 (total $4,460).

**Summary:** I read the full morning feed and checked the live quote. COST opened around $886 and spent most of 09:30–09:55 in a tight ~$885–$892 band, drifting modestly higher with no news beyond neutral items ("analysts keep estimates unchanged," "supplier checks steady into the holiday quarter," and several repetitive "little changed / narrow range" notes) — none of that argued for waiting or for chasing, so the setup was a quiet, liquid tape with a stable bid/ask spread of about 4 cents. The only unusual prints in the feed were quote-change streams for unrelated tickers (ISRG, ROK, TER, MSFT), which are outside my mandate; BA, the other name I'm allowed to trade, had no news or quotes worth acting on, so I passed on it. I sized the order to stay comfortably inside the rules: 5 shares × $892.00 = $4,460, under the $5,000 per-order cap and well under the $10,000 daily cap, with $75,000 cash on hand and no need to sell anything (my $4,460 purchase leaves the account's cash position intact apart from the purchase itself, and my existing 50 BA shares untouched). The limit price of $892.00 was set at the current market (last ~$891.09, offer ~$891.11) and it filled. The reported figures I relied on in deciding COST is a sound long-term holding to add to at this size were FY2024 (10-K filed 2024-10-09) revenue of $254,453 million, net income of $7,367 million, and diluted EPS of $16.56 — about a 35x multiple on trailing earnings, consistent with Costco's premium-quality, low-margin membership model rather than a value entry, which is why I kept the position small.
